title: Aprocitentan: Breakthrough Blood Pressure Treatment for Black Adults
text:
Facing the challenge of uncontrolled blood pressure? This article delves into the promising results of a new treatment, aprocitentan, specifically for Black adults struggling with resistant hypertension . Discover how this novel medication is showing potential in reducing blood pressure, minimizing proteinuria, and improving the lives of those most at risk, alongside expert insights on its impact.
Aprocitentan Shows Promise in Treating Resistant Hypertension in Black Adults April 9, 2025
aprocitentan ( Tryvio ; Idorsia ) has demonstrated significant blood pressure reductions in Black adults with resistant hypertension, according to a new study. The drug also reduced proteinuria and was well-tolerated, even in patients with chronic kidney disease.
Key Findings at a Glance Blood Pressure Reduction: Aprocitentan considerably lowered blood pressure in Black adults with resistant hypertension, even when added to existing antihypertensive regimens. Proteinuria Reduction: The drug reduced proteinuria in participants with elevated urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) at baseline. Safety and Tolerability: Aprocitentan was safe and well-tolerated, including in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The PRECISION Study: A Closer Look the findings are from a preplanned analysis of the phase 3 PRECISION study, published in the journal hypertension [[1]] . The study (NCT03541174) involved participants with a seated systolic BP (SBP) of 140 mm hg or greater,despite treatment with at least 3 antihypertensive medications [[1]] . More than half were taking 4 antihypertensive agents.
Study Design Participants were randomly assigned to receive aprocitentan 12.5 mg,25 mg,or placebo once daily during a 4-week double-blind period,followed by a 32-week single-arm period where all patients received aprocitentan 25 mg [[1]] .
Key Results The analysis included 82 participants who self-identified as Black. Key results include:
office SBP Reduction: During the initial 4-week period,the least-squares mean reduction in office SBP at trough level was -11.3 mm Hg (12.5 mg), -11.19 mm Hg (25 mg), and -12.0 mm Hg (placebo) [[1]] . Ambulatory BP Monitoring: 24-hour ambulatory systolic BP monitoring showed dose-dependent decreases at week 4 in aprocitentan-treated participants of -4.0 mm Hg (12.5 mg), -8.6 mm Hg (25 mg), and -0.7 mm Hg (placebo) [[1]] . The BP lowering effect was observed during both day and nighttime monitoring. Sustained BP Reduction: The mean systolic BP reduction from baseline continued, reaching 16.4 mm Hg at week 36 [[1]] . UACR Reduction: Aprocitentan reduced UACR by approximately 38% (12.5 mg) and 65% (25 mg) at week 4 in patients with micro- or macroalbuminuria,compared to a 13% reduction in the placebo group. these reductions in proteinuria were sustained throughout the study [[1]] . Safety and Tolerability Aprocitentan was well-tolerated in Black patients, including those with CKD [[1]] . Six patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events (AEs), with edema and fluid retention being the most commonly reported AEs during early treatment. No new safety signals emerged during long-term exposure.
Expert Insights Experts emphasize the relevance of these findings given the high burden of resistant hypertension among Black individuals, who experience disproportionately increased cardiovascular risk and lower rates of BP control [[1]] . The endothelin (ET) system is believed to play a key role in the pathogenesis of resistant hypertension, notably in populations prone to salt-sensitive and low-renin hypertension, as Black individuals tend to be.
Now, for the first time, we have an approved treatment targeting the endothelin system that may help fulfill an unmet need in Black patients with resistant hypertension.
Keith C. Ferdinand, MD, the Gerald S.Berenson Chair in Preventative Cardiology and professor of medicine at Tulane University School of medicine
dr.Ferdinand’s statement highlights the potential of aprocitentan to address a critical unmet need [[1]] .
Black adults with hypertension less frequently enough achieve guideline-recommended BP goals, leading to an estimated 400,000 cardiovascular events over 10 years that are preventable if control is achieved. In PRECISION, the effect of aprocitentan for these patients was striking.
John M. Flack, MD, MPH, chair of medicine at southern Illinois University School of Medicine
Dr. Flack emphasizes the significant impact aprocitentan could have on reducing cardiovascular events in this population [[1]] .
FDA Update: REMS Requirement Removed In a separate announcement on April 9, 2025, Idorsia reported that the FDA updated the aprocitentan label, removing the previous Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) requirement [[3]] .The agency determined that the benefits of aprocitentan outweigh the risks, including concerns about embryo-fetal toxicity.
References Idorsia News Release: Aprocitentan for Reducing Blood Pressure and Proteinuria in Black Patients Flack JM, Schlaich MP, Weber MA, et al. Aprocitentan for blood pressure reduction in Black patients. Hypertension . 2025;82(4):601-610. doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.124.24142
